messages:
maria.chen: FYI we just got a DSAR from an EU customer asking for account data + generation logs. Legal flagged a possible retention exception for some archived snapshots, asking if we can surface records before starting deletion.
raj.patel: do we need to temporarily unlock the keystore to decrypt archived embeddings for review? or can we provide proof without decrypting?
legal-sara: ideally no decryption unless absolutely required. they asked for "full dataset". we need to confirm scope. if decryption is needed, we need an approval chain and an auditable window.
kevin_w: technically the archived snapshots are KMS-wrapped with the customer keystore. we can grant a short-lived role to the dsar team to call Decrypt on specific objects, but KMS audit will show calls. need RBAC change + breakglass approval.
maria.chen: ok. proposal: create a timeboxed service-account role `dsar-temp-access` with 2-hour TTL, limited to the specific S3 prefix and KMS key id, and require 2 approvers (legal + security). audit log retention must be bumped to 7 years for this action. thoughts?
raj.patel: that sounds reasonable. we should also enable request tracing so we can link S3 reads -> KMS Decrypt -> API calls in one correlation id.
kevin_w: agree. implementation checklist: 1) IAM role with condition `aws:RequestTag/dsar_correlation_id` 2) KMS key policy allow `Decrypt` for role 3) S3 policy restrict prefix 4) temp token via STS with duration 2h.
olivia_s: please add a manual step to snapshot audit logs before granting access, plus an immutable artifact for legal.
incident-bot: Ticket #CS-8421 created for DSAR data access request (assignees: raj.patel, kevin_w, olivia_s). Approvals pending.
maria.chen: quick question re: audit logging — does our KMS integration currently log principal attributes (id/email) in the CloudTrail entry, or do we only get role ARNs? need something human-readable for legal.
kevin_w: CloudTrail gives the IAM principal ARN; we can augment by adding a mapping service in the ops audit pipeline that resolves ARNs -> employee identity at ingestion time. we already do this for deploys. will add for KMS events.
raj.patel: also add an HMAC'd proof bundle that contains the correlation id, manifest of objects accessed, and a signed hash we store in the legal evidence bucket. example manifest format: ```
{
  "correlation_id": "dsar-1743123456-a1b2",
  "accessed_objects": ["s3://redwood-archive/customer-12345/snap-2022-09-01.tar.gz"],
  "kms_key_id": "arn:aws:kms:eu:111:alias/customer-12345-key",
  "timestamp": "2024-10-08T15:00:00Z"
}
```
legal-sara: perfect, that satisfies chain-of-custody needs. make sure the evidence bucket is write-once (object lock) and access is limited to legal+security.
maria.chen: on RBAC approvals, I'll start a formal Slack approval thread with @legal-sara and @olivia_s for sign-off. after both sign, infra will perform the short-lived grant.
kevin_w: implementation note — we should avoid changing the KMS key policy permanently. use a temporary grant (KMS CreateGrant) and schedule automatic revoke after TTL. KMS grants show up in audit and are easy to revoke.
raj.patel: good call. also set CloudWatch alarm if there's >10 Decrypt calls in the 2h window to catch accidental mass decrypts.
olivia_s: ops will run the job at 09:00 UTC tomorrow if approvals land today. I'll attach the runbook to the ticket.
maria.chen: one more: data minimization check — if any of the archived objects contain unrelated PII, we must redact before providing. who owns redaction?
legal-sara: legal owns scope, engineering does redaction. assume minimal disclosure. if redaction impossible, escalate to data-privacy lead for exception.
kevin_w: noted. I'll draft the automation to copy objects to a staging bucket, run redaction lambda (opt-out rules), then grant decryption on the staged objects only.
raj.patel: linking to retention exception: if legal deems some items under exception (e.g., litigation hold), DO NOT delete. we need a manifest of those items.
maria.chen: ok team — next steps: 1) legal confirm scope + approvers (legal-sara) 2) infra implement temp grant + manifest & proof pipeline (kevin, raj) 3) ops run staging + redaction (olivia) 4) attach evidence to ticket and call out retention exceptions. target to complete within 48h.
legal-sara: approved the approach. please add me to the approval flow. :white_check_mark:
kevin_w: I'll open a PR with IAM policy snippets and the KMS CreateGrant pattern. pinging here when ready.
raj.patel: PR linked and infra test run succeeded in staging. logs: `Decrypt=1, S3GetObject=1` for the correlation id.
maria.chen: thanks all. closing the slack thread — we'll update ticket CS-8421 with final artifacts. :lock:
